about.title: Tulare Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Slip and fall incidents happen throughout Tulare — in the parking lots along Blackstone, inside stores near Bardsley, or on stairwells at rental properties tucked off SR-99. What separates a strong claim from a weak one usually comes down to proof: was there a spill left unattended, a broken step nobody repaired, poor lighting in a stairwell? Under California law, the property owner or manager generally has to have known, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to correct it or warn visitors. That's why documenting conditions immediately and requesting surveillance footage before it's erased matters so much. We evaluate the details of your case and pursue the claim on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless money is recovered.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Fall

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California law generally requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. We know how to gather inspection records, employee statements, and maintenance logs to establish this.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Tulare businesses overwrite security video within days or weeks. Acting quickly to preserve that footage can be the difference between a documented hazard and a dispute over what happened.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Recovery
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly blamed for not seeing a hazard, you may still recover a reduced amount. We can push back on unfair fault arguments from a property's insurer.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Tulare?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is government-owned, such as a public building near Rt 137, the deadline is much shorter and requires a separate claims process. It's best to have us review the timeline as soon as possible.

items.question: What if I fell at a store and didn't report it right away?
items.answer: It's better to report a fall as soon as it happens, but a delayed report doesn't automatically end your claim. What matters most is being able to show the hazard existed and that the property owner had notice of it. We can help gather evidence even after the fact, like requesting incident logs or footage.

items.question: Will my claim be reduced if I was partly at fault?
items.answer: Possibly, but not eliminated. California's pure comparative fault rule means your recovery can be reduced by your percentage of fault rather than barred completely. This applies whether the fall happened at a Tulare shopping center, apartment complex, or elsewhere.
